subject: Matematik
title: Probability and statistics
sourceSummary: Measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode), single- and two-step probability, and combinatorics.

questions.prompt: What is the mean of the numbers 4, 7, 9 and 12?
questions.opener: Add everything together first — then divide by something.

questions.prompt: What is the median of the number sequence 3, 5, 8, 9, 12?
questions.opener: The median is about the middle position, not about calculating something.
questions.explanation: The numbers are already in order and there are five of them, so the median is the third one: 8.

questions.prompt: What is the median of the number sequence 2, 4, 6, 10?
questions.opener: An even number of values — so there's no single middle point.
questions.explanation: With an even number of values, you take the mean of the two middle ones: $(4 + 6)/2 = 5$.

questions.prompt: You roll a standard six-sided die. What is the probability of getting a four?
questions.opener: How many outcomes are favourable, and how many are possible in total?
questions.explanation: One favourable outcome (the four) out of six possible: $\frac{1}{6} \approx 17\ \%$.

questions.prompt: A bag contains 3 red and 7 blue marbles. You draw one marble without looking. What is the probability that it is red?
questions.opener: How many marbles are there in total in the bag?
questions.explanation: 10 marbles in total, of which 3 are red: $\frac{3}{10} = 0{,}3 = 30\ \%$.

questions.prompt: You have 3 tops and 4 pairs of trousers. How many different combinations can you put together?
questions.opener: For each top — how many trousers can you choose to go with it?
questions.explanation: Each top can be combined with all four pairs of trousers: $3 \cdot 4 = 12$ combinations.

questions.prompt: You flip a coin twice. What is the probability of getting heads both times? Show your reasoning.
questions.opener: What is the probability of heads in one flip — and how do you combine two independent events?
steps: The probability of heads in one flip is $\frac{1}{2}$.
The flips don't affect each other, so the probabilities are multiplied.
Check: the four equally likely outcomes are HH, HT, TH, TT — one out of four gives two heads.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between mean, median and mode.
questions.opener: Three different ways of answering the question "what is typical?".
questions.answer: Mean: the sum of all the values divided by how many there are. Median: the middle value once they've been sorted in order (the mean of the two middle values when there's an even number). Mode: the value that occurs most often. The median is the least affected by extreme values.

questions.prompt: What is the mode of the data set 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 7, 7, 9?
questions.opener: The mode is the value that occurs most often — count how many times each number appears.
questions.explanation: The number 7 occurs three times, more than any other number in the data set (3 occurs twice, 5 and 9 once each).

questions.prompt: The mean of five test scores is 74. Four of the scores are 68, 70, 75 and 80. What is the fifth score?
questions.opener: Work out what the sum of all five must be, then subtract the four you know.
questions.explanation: The sum of all five: $74 \cdot 5 = 370$. The four known: $68 + 70 + 75 + 80 = 293$. The fifth: $370 - 293 = 77$.

questions.prompt: You draw a card from a standard deck of 52 cards. What is the probability that it is a heart (13 cards out of four suits)?
questions.opener: How many of the 52 cards are hearts?

questions.prompt: The probability that it rains tomorrow is 35 %. What is the probability that it does NOT rain?
questions.opener: The two outcomes (rain or no rain) must together add up to 100 %.

questions.prompt: A menu has 4 starters, 5 main courses and 3 desserts. How many different three-course meals (one of each) can you put together?
questions.opener: Multiply the number of choices at each step.
questions.explanation: $4 \cdot 5 \cdot 3 = 60$. All three steps must be multiplied together, not just two of them.

questions.prompt: In a class of 30 students, 18 have siblings. If you randomly pick a student, what is the probability that the student does NOT have siblings? Show your reasoning.
questions.opener: First work out how many students have no siblings.

questions.prompt: A group has the monthly salaries (in thousands of kr) 25, 27, 28, 26 and 95. Which statement is true?
questions.opener: Work out both the mean and the median, and compare how the extreme value 95 affects them.
choices: The mean is a better picture of a typical salary because it takes all the values into account.
The median (27) gives a better picture of a typical salary than the mean (40,2), because 95 pulls the mean up.
The mean and the median are the same size in this group.
The mode is the most representative measure here.
questions.explanation: The mean is $(25+27+28+26+95)/5 = 40{,}2$, but the median (the middle value in 25, 26, 27, 28, 95) is only 27. The extreme value 95 pulls up the mean but does not affect the median as much. There is no mode here since no number repeats.
